quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which part of the lane is safest?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
It depends on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Move your position in the lane based on conditions around you.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Bright-colored clothing so other drivers can see you.
Any color, because daylight makes you easy to see.
Dark-colored clothing to stand out against the sun.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothing so other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors to be more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: The biggest danger is at intersections. Most crashes happen when cars turn left in front of motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
You will get through the turn faster.
You will keep better control of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Turning too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: When can motorcycles pass on the right?

options.text: If there are at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on the grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there are at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: How high can motorcycle handlebars be?

options.text: Even with the seat.
No more than 15 inches above the seat.
No higher than your head when sitting.

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than 15 inches above the seat.
questions.explanation: Handlebars cannot be more than 15 inches higher than the seat.

questions.question: Where should you ride when it is raining?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain starts. Ride in tire tracks left by cars for better grip.

questions.question: What is one thing proper riding clothes do NOT do?

options.text: Protect you in a crash.
Protect you from weather.
Help you blend in with other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you blend in with other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in crashes and from weather. It also makes you more visible, so blending in is not a benefit.

questions.question: If you wear a helmet in a crash, are you more likely to survive?

options.text: No, you are less likely to survive.
No, you have the same chance as without a helmet.
Yes, you are more likely to survive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you are more likely to survive.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel locks while stopping?

options.text: Keep pressing the front brake.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the front brake immediately. Then press it firmly again. Use both brakes together when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather
Wool
Any soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar tough material. This gives you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid talking and moving unnecessarily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking and moving unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move unless needed while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.

options.text: Louder than
Quieter than
About as loud as

questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as car horns. You can use your horn when needed, but do not depend on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid areas with heavy traffic.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Watch the road well ahead of you to spot dangers before you reach them. This gives you time to react and avoid trouble.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of staying far away from other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles helps you react to dangers and move out of the way if needed. This extra space is not about having time to speed up in curves.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up.
The same amount of time to stop and speed up.
More time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows down acceleration and braking. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly when carrying a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, you should usually:

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight across the tracks in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across the tracks in your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled railroad tracks. Turning to change your angle may move you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:

options.text: Has no cracks or defects.
Looks nice.
Fits loosely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It should fit snugly and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: One
Two
Three

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one drink can reduce your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Your body removes alcohol at what rate?

options.text: About one drink per hour.
About two drinks per hour.
About three drinks per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour on average. This varies by person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an object?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Lean your motorcycle.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and approach it at a 90-degree angle. Keep your motorcycle straight. Rise slightly off your seat. Roll on the throttle just before you hit it.

questions.question: When parked on the road, how should a motorcycle be positioned?

options.text: At a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb.
Without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts or tricks to speed up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best protection. They should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to change to red.
The light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the light will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles travel at less than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn carts.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.
0.3 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In California, it is illegal to ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher if you are 21 or older. If you are under 21, the legal limit is 0.01 percent. It may be unsafe to ride even if you are below the legal limit.
